Subject: Post-demo follow-up: perf targets & next steps
Attachments: Sparrow-perf-numbers.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo today — appreciate the clear walkthrough of the Redwood routing and dedicated options. Per our conversation, here are the key performance requirements from our infra/engineering side: 

- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 200ms for single-turn short responses (~120 tokens)
- Throughput: sustained 100 requests/sec during business hours (PST) with spikes to 250 req/s for short bursts
- Concurrency: up to 50 concurrent interactive sessions (concurrent streams)
- Streaming: yes — we need partial tokens streamed to front-end to reduce perceived latency
- Model class: open to 7B/13B variants; prefer lower-cost quantized 4-bit if quality holds

I attached a workbook with our current traffic profile and sample payload sizes. High-level asks: can Redwood meet the p95 target with streaming enabled, and what cost levers would you recommend to hit SLO while keeping monthly spend reasonable?

Next steps we discussed: perf test with our sample workload, a short MAP, and an estimate for peak capacity. Can you confirm availability for a perf test next week (Mon/Tue preferred)?

Thanks — Liam
Liam Chen
Director, Platform Engineering | Sparrow Health

Hi Liam — great to talk and thanks for the spreadsheet. I pulled out the key targets below to make sure we’re aligned: 

- p95 <= 200ms (120-token responses)
- sustained 100 req/s, bursts to 250 req/s
- concurrency 50 (concurrent streaming sessions)
- streaming required

We can run a perf test next Tue (2026-03-02) morning PT — does 9:30am PT work for your infra team?

Quick answers to your questions on hitting the SLO while controlling cost:
- Continuous batching: will reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead for high throughput; we'll tune batch size and latency windows during the perf run.
- KV/prefix caching: ideal for repeated prompts (chat history) — reduces compute by serving cached KV cache or partial prefixes.
- Quantization profiles: recommend starting with an 8-bit (Q8) profile for 13B for quality safety, test 4-bit (Q4) variants to see if quality holds for your prompts.
- Model variants & fallback: start with a 13B quantized model for the main path and fall back to cheaper 7B for non-critical workloads.

I attached a draft MAP with goals, owners, and timelines. Rishi/Priyom: can you add an initial config suggestion for the perf run (instance types, concurrency settings, batching windows, and a rough cost estimate)?

Liam — if you can confirm Tue 9:30am PT and share a test account + sample payloads (or the Drive folder link), we’ll lock it in.

Best,
Marissa

Liam / Marissa — quick technical summary + proposed perf-run config so everyone has visibility. Happy to discuss further during the perf test.

TL;DR: We can meet p95 <= 200ms with streaming if we use dedicated capacity with these levers: continuous batching, aggressive KV caching, and a tuned quantization profile. Estimated starting capacity ~2x of sustained load to cover burst absorption and background overhead.

Proposed perf-run configuration (initial):
- Model: 13B open checkpoint, Q8 initial; test Q4 with eval set (quality/regression checks)
- Deployment: Dedicated pool (2 nodes to start), GPU type: A100-80GB or equivalent for stable KV cache + higher batch throughput
- Batching: continuous batching window 20-30ms targeting median latency tradeoff; dynamic batch-size up to 64 for token generation when traffic aggregates
- Concurrency & routing: limit per-worker concurrency to ~8 streams, shard sessions across multiple workers; router policy to prioritize streaming/low-latency requests on lower-util nodes
- Caching: prefix + KV cache for repeated prompts; enable local LRU cache size tuned to session history (we'll estimate based on your payloads)
- Fallbacks: 7B Q4 variant for background tasks and non-streaming endpoints to save cost

Rough cost tradeoffs (monthly estimate, highly dependent on usage):
- Baseline (dedicated, Q8 13B): $Xk/month for capacity to sustain 100 req/s with 2x headroom
- With Q4 fallback and aggressive caching: ~25–40% lower per-token cost; continuous batching can shave another ~15% on throughput-heavy workloads

Test plan for Tue 9:30am PT:
1) Run ramp test 0 -> 100 req/s sustained (10m), then 250 req/s burst (2m)
2) Capture p50/p95/p99, stream latency breakdown (first-byte, token-arrival), and GPU utilization/KV hit rate
3) Iterate batching window and node count in 20-min blocks to find best latency-cost point

Action items: 
- Marissa to confirm perf-run time and provide test credentials + sample payloads (Liam)
- Priyom to prepare perf harness config and keep a small pre-seeded KV cache for repeated prompts
- Rishi to join test and iterate on batching/quantization knobs

Priyom: I’ll leave the low-level perf-config to you (instance sizing, exact autoscale headroom, and logging hooks).

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
